purpose: Proves bounded interprocedural registrar-following: same-package function, cross-package function, method-value registrar, the idiomatic if-err/plain-assign/return-delegation control-flow shapes for an error-returning registrar, and one genuinely unresolvable case (callback held in a function-typed parameter) that must diagnose rather than silently drop.

excludedRoutes.note: registered inside a callback passed as a function-typed parameter; not followed

expectedDiagnostics.note: cb(r) inside registerViaCallback — cb is a parameter, not a resolvable function/method reference

controlFlowExpectedRoutes.note: via if err := registerViaIfErr(r); err != nil { ... } — found silently missed on a real production service (120 routes hidden) because walkStmt never visited IfStmt.Init
via err := registerViaPlainAssign(r) — found silently missed because handleAssign never fell through to tryFollowRegistrarCall for a non-engine/group RHS call
via return registerViaReturn(r) inside wrapReturnedRegistrar — found silently missed because walkStmt never visited ReturnStmt
